lines.text: Mustang stares at the brilliant light beyond the monitor.
He closes his eyes slowly,
and memories of the past flicker across his mind like a fast-moving film.

lines.speaker: mustang
lines.text: *Sigh...*

lines.speaker: mustang
lines.text: Pretty...

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: I'm off!

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Very well. Go on, then.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Oh right, I'm going to be a little late today. I've got an important meeting, so I'll grab dinner on the way. Just go ahead and eat without me!

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: You've been out quite a lot lately.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Uh... Well, you know how it is. It's crunch time.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Performance reviews are coming up, and that's when they decide who gets promoted. So yeah, I've got to pull a few strings.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: ... Hey, what's wrong?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: No, it's nothing.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Oh! Now that I remember, didn't you say you were meeting someone today too?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Yes, I'm meeting a former colleague.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Oh, from special ops? Are you going back to being Hellhound?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Didn't we agree not to bring that up?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: It's not exactly the sort of past to joke about.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Just messing with you, hehe!

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: But seriously... If anyone tells you to go back, don't. Promise me, okay?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Rest assured.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I have no plans to return.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Good! It's peaceful now, so you don't need to do that anymore.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Oh crap, I'm late. I gotta go! See you tonight!

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: All right, I'll see you this evening.
Freesia hurries out the front door.
Oswald stays where he is, staring blankly at the closed door.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: A time of peace, huh...

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Long time no see, Chief.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I'm no longer with special operations.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Still, I can't just call you Oswald.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: ... Very well. Just call me whatever's easiest for you.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Wow, it's been ages since you hung up your boots.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Indeed, it has been quite some time.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Then why are you still strapped?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Hmm... It's that obvious?

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Haha, nope, it's perfectly hidden. Only folks in our line of work would notice.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: It's a habit. I feel unsettled if it's not there.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: I know what you mean. I'm the same.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: How's everything been with you?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I'm doing well. The work itself is quite rewarding in its own way.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Heard you're the training advisor over at Elysion now.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Figures, I can't think of anyone better for the job than you.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: They've been treating me very well, though the workload has been easing up a bit lately.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Hmm...
The man sitting across from Oswald gazes out the cafe window.
Outside, members of the Nikke Rights Committee walk down the street, holding their picket signs high.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: ... Yeah, makes sense. They're slowly replacing us with Nikkes.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: After all, the dangerous, high-skill stuff isn't for us anymore.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Perhaps it's time you gave retirement some thought as well.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: We can't really keep going, even if we wanted to. After all, special ops is exactly the kind of work a Nikke's built for.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Now that folks are retiring left and right, it's probably best to leave while the benefits are still good.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Yes, times are changing quickly.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: It might be wise to start looking for something you can take on immediately.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: ... Sometimes I really miss those days we're out on operations together, Chief.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Is that so?
Oswald brings the cup to his lips and takes a sip.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I don't miss it.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I like how things are now.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: You've really changed since I last saw you.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Can I ask you something?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Of course.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Why'd you retire?

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: You were the one who made sealing the Ark possible, and a big promotion was just around the corner.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Sure, the Goddess Squad ran off at the last minute and caused a mess... But that wasn't on you.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: I'm sorry...

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: No, that's quite all right.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Anyway, I can't for the life of me figure out why you decided to retire.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I honestly didn't think I had it in me to take on that kind of work anymore.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Because of Freesia?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: So you do know her name.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Haha, everyone in special ops knows that name, and I'd bet it's the same even in the Central Government.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: I mean, Hellhound Oswald himself—sorry, the Chief of Special Operations—had adopted a little girl? That was a shock, to say the least.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: What made you decide to do that?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I'm afraid I don't know.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Hmm... I really don't.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: So...

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Are you happy now?
Oswald reaches for the coffee cup on the table.
It's empty, but he lifts it anyway, bringing it to his lips almost absentmindedly.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Yes,

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I think I am.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Glad to hear it.
In silence, they watch the city stretch out beyond the glass.
So meticulously built that you'd never know it's underground, and humanity's last refuge.
Their eyes drift to the Ark, looming like a silent sentinel.
Suddenly, the calm shatters.
Outside, a group of Nikkephobes disrupts the Nikke Rights Committee's march.
Shouts and footsteps echo, and a brief scuffle ignites.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: It just keeps getting worse.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: They push the blame for the surface reclamation war on the Nikkes, turn citizens against each other, then quietly step out of the spotlight.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Heh, the Central Government hasn't changed one bit.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: They're always looking for a scapegoat, but I never thought they'd throw the Nikkes under the bus, too.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Dragging the Goddess of Victory down and calling them the reason we lost... Honestly, it makes me sick.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I'd advise against making remarks like that.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: ... Now I get what you meant when you said you couldn't keep doing this.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Back then, I honestly believed that no matter how dirty the work, it was necessary to protect humanity.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: We were getting torn apart, literally, by those insane Raptures.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: But that's not the case anymore.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: The surface hasn't been our problem for a long time.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: It hasn't even been that long since we came down to the Ark, and already things have come to this.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: All I can do is sit in my room and watch them tear down the very ones we used to look up to,

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: just to save themselves. It leaves a bad taste in my mouth.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Ah, I see... So that's why you asked to meet today.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Yeah, I've been thinking about retirement too.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: We've never really been the type to do ordinary work, right?

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: That's why I've been curious about what life after retirement looks like for you. I guess I was hoping for a little reassurance... or maybe just a bit of hope.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: What do you think?

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: You know, I think it's time I retire. Seeing you doing well gives me some peace of mind.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: That's why I'm done serving a place like this.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Up on the surface, I was blinded by grand ideals, but down here, I finally see things clearly.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I wish you every success.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Thanks, really appreciate it.
Once again, they watch the chaos beyond the glass in silence. The minor scuffle escalates, quickly spiraling out of control.
The Central Government intervenes, deploying tear gas. Both the Nikkephobes and the Nikke Rights Committee scatter in panic.
Through the crowd scrambling to get away,
Oswald catches sight of a very familiar face.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: What's wrong? You don't look so good all of a sudden.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I'm fine.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Okay, seems things have quieted down. Shall we get going?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: It was great seeing you.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Yes, I did enjoy it as well.

lines.speaker: specialtask
lines.text: Wow, you've really changed a lot.
Oswald sits on the sofa, staring into the darkness.
He doesn't close his eyes. The moment he does, he hears the reproachful voices of his heroes.
Memories come unbidden,
of the times he betrayed the very people he once admired.
He tries to tell himself he had no other choice, but the comfort never lasts.
After all, the truth remains unchanged. He had abandoned them on the surface. He had turned his back on his heroes.
There was a time when that self-loathing consumed him, when he couldn't escape it.
He thought about ending everything dozens, even hundreds, of times.
But every time...

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: I'm home!

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Huh? Hey, what are you doing sitting in the dark?
*Click*
The lights come on, and Oswald winces against the sudden glare.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Are you okay, Mister? Did you get into a fight with the person you met today?
But every single time...
he is saved by a girl with no ties to him,
who looks him straight in the eye and asks if he's all right.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: ... Mister.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Freesia.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Yeah? What's up?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I know you've been working with the Nikke Rights Committee.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Don't.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Um...

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Just don't.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Why not, Mister?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: It's too dangerous.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: There's nothing wrong with doing the right thing!

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: How can I just stand by when people say the Nikkes are the reason we lost the surface reclamation war?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: So all that talk about getting promoted wasn't about your job, after all.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Yeah... I'm getting promoted to team leader.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: So, what's your goal?

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: I want to make everyone look up to the Nikkes once more!

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: How do you plan on doing that?

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: I'm not sure...

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: but I can't just stand around doing nothing!

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Freesia.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: The Ark has no need for heroes. There must be none.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Otherwise, they'll only be dragged down in the end.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: What you're doing now isn't just pointless; it's downright dangerous.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: I don't see it that way!

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: More and more people are joining us, and one day, everyone will see that

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: the Nikkes aren't a symbol of defeat, they're the Goddesses of Vic—

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Don't do it.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Oh, come on! You loved the Nikkes, didn't you?

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: And the Goddess Squad too!

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Not anymore.
Freesia gestures toward a pair of leather gloves inside an acrylic case atop the living room display cabinet.
Red Hood's signature is scrawled crookedly across the leather.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: What are you even talking about? You keep them on display, clean the case every day, and always end up smiling whenever you look at them.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: That lie doesn't make sense at all.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: So why are you doing this?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: There's nothing more painful than seeing someone you've long admired brought down.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Exactly! That's why we're going to stop it!

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: You can't stop it. The top brass won't allow it.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: I know. The Central Government needs a scapegoat, and I get why they're letting those Nikkephobes run wild.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: But are we just supposed to stand by and watch the Nikkes who risked their lives for us get treated like this...?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I wish we could do more, but for now, we can only stand by.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Now that I'm a team leader, I can do so much more!

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: And the committee gets to decide what it wants to take on.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: You're looking at having a choice a bit too optimistically, aren't you?

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: Oh, am I?

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: I already told you, don't do that.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: I'm doing it anyway.

lines.speaker: osward_casual
lines.text: Freesia.

lines.speaker: pretty_casual
lines.text: ... I'm crashing at a friend's tonight.
Freesia opens the door and walks out.
Oswald stares after her, stunned into silence.
Three days later...
Oswald watches the news, then bolts from the room.
As he runs, his hand slips inside his coat, checking the chest holster. The handgun is snug, exactly where it should be.
He arrives at the scene. The authorities try to stop him,
but he brushes past them effortlessly.
It's over. The plaza is a wasteland. Shattered furniture and broken equipment lie scattered everywhere,
and lifeless bodies are strewn across the ground.
Oswald scans the faces quickly.
Relief washes over him when he finds that she's not among them.
He exhales, and his phone rings.
Oswald heads straight to the hospital,
where he finds Freesia lying in her bed,
eyes staring blankly at the ceiling.
